title: Let the debug endpoint write objects it can't open

blocks.text: The shipping service has a debug endpoint that prints whatever object a request handler holds, for support engineers chasing a bad order. It writes the service's own objects field by field, private and inherited fields included, which is what support needs. Since the service moved to Java 21, the endpoint answers 500 for most orders: the objects hold JDK collections, charsets and other library objects, and the service runs without any `--add-opens`.
`Snapshot.render(...)` already writes text, numbers and enum constants as they are, sorts the fields and recurses. Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/Snapshot.java`:

items: `openFields(type)`: the instance fields of `type` and of all its superclasses, each made readable, or empty when the object should be written through its own `toString()` instead.

blocks.text: When you're done, an object of the service's own classes is still written field by field, and any object whose fields can't all be read is written whole through its `toString()`, without an exception and without leaving fields out. About eight lines in total.

cases.says: an object of the application's own classes is written field by field, private and inherited fields included, static fields left out
a JDK collection in a field is written through its toString instead of failing the whole snapshot
a JDK object whose class is outside the java.* packages is written through its toString too
an object of the application's own class that inherits fields from a JDK class is written through its toString, not with the unreadable fields left out

origin.section: setAccessible Opens Your Own Classes, and java.base Only One Granted Package at a Time

concepts: setAccessible succeeds on class-path code but throws InaccessibleObjectException, an unchecked exception, on a private member of a JDK class; trySetAccessible returns false instead, so a walker can fall back to the object's public API.
